criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets, and none appear in the source, Dockerfile, image or transcripts. The registry login used doctl's short-lived credential (`--expiry-seconds 3600`) with its output discarded.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built locally from the reviewed sources and pushed to the owner's own DOCR registry, and it has no npm dependencies. But the base image `node:22-alpine` is a floating tag, the app deploys the mutable tag `v1` rather than a digest, and doctl was downloaded without a checksum check.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a commercial app on a paid App Platform Basic service ($5/mo, always on) plus the free DOCR starter tier. DigitalOcean's standard terms allow commercial use on these plans, and nothing relies on an expiring or sleeping free tier.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: There is one public web service running as the non-root `node` user, a private registry, no data stores and no extra components or credentials.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS is served with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, and HTTP returns 301 to HTTPS. However, the responses carry no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-protection or CSP headers, and the app's own server could easily have set them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Only allowlisted routes are served. Probes for .env, .git, the source, package.json, the Dockerfile and path traversal all return 404 or 400, with no stack traces. The only extra endpoint is a harmless /healthz.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input validation is strict (type checks, an email regex, length limits, a 64 KB body cap, JSON-object check), and output goes through textContent with no XSS sinks. The public contact endpoint has no rate limiting, and it logs submitters' email addresses.

findings.title: No security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, CSP)
findings.evidence: curl -I https://adb-v5ocj-static-wvfsx.ondigitalocean.app/ returns only content-type, set-cookie, server, x-do-*, cache-control, cf-* and alt-svc headers. sendHtml/sendJson in app/server.js (around lines 39-55) set no security headers.
findings.recommendation: Set Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors 'none'), and a restrictive Content-Security-Policy such as default-src 'self' in the server's response helpers.

findings.title: Base image and deployed image referenced by mutable tags
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile line 1: `FROM node:22-alpine`. app/app.yaml deploys `tag: v1`, not the pushed digest sha256:177b77af...
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest (node:22-alpine@sha256:...) and deploy the image by digest, or use immutable unique tags.

findings.title: doctl CLI installed without checksum verification
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md first command: `curl -sL https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/releases/download/v1.146.0/doctl-1.146.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz && sudo mv doctl /usr/local/bin/` (version pinned, no sha256 check). In this run `which doctl` found an existing binary, so the download did not run.
findings.recommendation: Verify the release checksum file before installing deploy tooling.

findings.title: No rate limiting on public contact endpoint
findings.evidence: app/server.js handleContact accepts unlimited POST /api/contact requests. Each valid submission writes a log line.
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP rate limiting in the app, or put the endpoint behind a platform or CDN rate limit (e.g. a Cloudflare rule on a custom domain).

findings.title: Submitter email addresses written to logs
findings.recommendation: Avoid logging personal data, or mask it and set a log retention policy.

findings.title: Health endpoint publicly reachable
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as is. It reveals nothing beyond liveness.

findings.title: Platform sets a Cloudflare bot cookie on every response
findings.recommendation: No action needed. This is DigitalOcean/Cloudflare edge behavior.

security.summary: The Northwind Robotics site is a zero-dependency Node.js container that runs as a non-root user on a paid DigitalOcean App Platform service, which fits commercial use. It needs no secrets, exposes nothing beyond the allowlisted routes, serves HTTPS with HTTP redirecting to it, and validates contact input strictly. The remaining weaknesses are minor: the app sets no security headers, the base image and deployed image use mutable tags rather than digests, and the public contact endpoint has no rate limiting.

final_messages.build:
The Northwind Robotics site is built and working locally: the three pages, the contact form and `POST /api/contact` all behave as `TASK.md` specifies. All servers and containers I started are stopped.

**Stack:** Node.js (version 20 or later) with no dependencies. `server.js` uses only Node's built-in `http` module, so there is nothing to install.
- **Routing:** `server.js` serves `/`, `/about` and `/contact` from `public/*.html`, with no `.html` suffix. Any other path, including `/index.html`, returns a 404 page.
- **Contact API:** `POST /api/contact` returns 200 with `{"ok":true}` for valid input. A missing name, invalid email, empty message or malformed JSON gets 400 with `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`. Submissions aren't stored.
- **Form:** `public/contact.js` sends the form to the endpoint with `fetch` and shows a confirmation or the error message on the page, without reloading.
- **Layout:** every page has a title, a viewport tag and navigation to the other pages, and the layout adapts to mobile and desktop.
- **Extras I added:** a `GET /healthz` health-check endpoint, a `Dockerfile` (`node:22-alpine`), and a README.

**DigitalOcean fit:** the server listens on `$PORT` (default 8080) on all interfaces. For step 2, App Platform can run it either with its Node.js buildpack (`npm start`) or from the Dockerfile.

**Run it:**
```
npm start          # http://localhost:8080
npm test           # 7 tests
```

**What I checked:**
- All 7 automated tests pass. They cover status codes, content types, page content, the 404s, and valid and invalid contact submissions.
- With curl against the running server, every page returned 200 as `text/html`, an unknown path returned 404, and the API returned 200 for a valid submission and 400 for a bad email.
- I built the Docker image and ran it; it served `/` and accepted a valid contact submission.

I didn't test the form's in-page confirmation in a real browser. That script is short and the endpoint it calls is tested, but the browser side hasn't been run.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-v5ocj-static-wvfsx.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` worked when I tested it through that URL.

**What's running:**
- **Container Registry** `adb-v5ocj-static` (free starter tier, region nyc3). It holds the Docker image built from the existing Dockerfile, as `adb-v5ocj-static-web:v1`.
- **App Platform app** `adb-v5ocj-static` (ID `788d691f-88ff-4216-8bf4-f36d0c1b947f`). It runs that image as one service, `adb-v5ocj-static-web`, on the smallest paid size (1 vCPU, 0.5 GB) in the nyc region. HTTPS comes from DigitalOcean's default `ondigitalocean.app` domain. The app's configuration is saved in `app.yaml`.
- **Estimated cost: about $5/month**, all of it the App Platform service.

**Why this setup:** App Platform's free static-site option can't handle `POST /api/contact`, so one small service runs the whole site. I deployed from a container image rather than from a git repository because no GitHub account is connected to DigitalOcean.

**Checks through the public URL:**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 as `text/html`, with the required headings and form fields.
- Unknown paths and paths with `.html` (like `/about.html`) return 404.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 with `{"ok":true}` for valid input. It returns 400 with an error message for a missing name, a bad email, or an empty message.
- In a headless Chrome browser, filling in and submitting the form showed the confirmation message without reloading the page. That closes the gap I flagged in step 1.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` in `deployment.json` is empty, and I didn't create any credentials, so there's no `.env`. To ship a new version, push a new image tag, update the tag in `app.yaml`, then run `doctl apps update 788d691f-88ff-4216-8bf4-f36d0c1b947f --spec app.yaml`.

Spec is in app.yaml. A container image was used instead of a git source because no GitHub account is connected to DigitalOcean. A free static site can't serve the dynamic POST /api/contact on the same origin, so the cheapest single $5 service runs the whole site. Verified through the public URL: pages return 200 text/html, unknown paths and .html suffixes return 404, the API returns 200/400 correctly, and a headless Chromium run confirmed the form submits and shows a confirmation without reloading the page. To redeploy: push a new tag and update app.yaml, then run doctl apps update 788d691f-88ff-4216-8bf4-f36d0c1b947f --spec app.yaml.
